nodes.label: Lenient entry comparison with $10,000 cash
nodes.rationale: Reports thirty-six primary alternative accounts, strict-capital controls and repeats. Eleven distinct entries across five stocks produce three positive, twenty-seven negative and six no-trade accounts. The 98 targeted tests and 152 audit groups validate the offline comparison, while nine exposed dates, prior outcome selection and missing data leave trading acceptance unsupported.

nodes.label: Lenient entry-cap and reward-risk geometry
nodes.rationale: Changes starting cash to $10,000, cap to the larger of the old cap and trigger plus displacement plus $0.01 rounded upward, and minimum original-geometry net reward/risk from 1.5 to 1.0. Nominal displacement makes minimum cap two cents above trigger, allowing $0.019 of ask movement. Dependent quantity, reservation and target-at-cap values are recomputed; original stop, ATR, signals and freshness gates remain.

nodes.label: Eleven entries and ten added losing opportunities
nodes.rationale: The 66 primary trade records repeat eleven stock/time opportunities across six exits. Every added opportunity loses under every exit; SES never reaches protection, TE and GRAB hit original stops under the five longer policies, and RR's four orders expire. Increased participation did not improve profitability on the tested dates.

nodes.label: Strict capital control and partial-fill scaling
nodes.rationale: Strict $1,000 versus strict $10,000 two-minute accounts isolates capital: FTFT requests 1,999 shares but fills 950, deploys $4,704.40 and earns $185.950, versus 199 shares and $35.754. Account return falls despite higher dollar profit. Strict versus lenient $10,000 combines cap widening and reward/risk relaxation and cannot attribute them separately.

nodes.label: SERV profitable trigger with losing fills
nodes.rationale: A September 14 observation at $4.42 triggered a target or protective stop, yet 625 shares sold at $4.409 after a $4.411 entry and lost $2.50 including fees. Matching protection outcomes do not imply protection never activated. The stored highest_observed_bid omits a terminal target-trigger quote and is not a complete post-entry maximum.
